My skin looks more awake and radiant thanks to the vitamin C, and I appreciate knowing I'm getting SPF 50 protection without that heavy sunscreen feel or smell. This is perfect for everyday wear, especially if you want brighter-looking skin while keeping things simple. It's been an easy reach for me and fits perfectly into a real-life, on-the-go routine.

avis.titre: Murad's Brightening SPF: My Skin's New Favorite Filter
avis.texte: Let's just say this: if sunshine and skincare had a baby, Murad's Superactive Moisturizer SPF 50 would be it. I was skeptical (as usual) when a friend swore this was her "glow-up in a bottle," but here I am—converted and glowing. First off, the texture? Smooth like silk but light enough to make you forget it's even there. No white cast. No greasy finish. Just a dewy, healthy-looking sheen that screams, "I drink water and mind my business." It absorbs like a dream and layers beautifully under makeup—no pilling, no weird patches, just vibes. The brightening effect is real, too. I noticed after about two weeks that my skin looked more even-toned and just… fresher. Not in a fake, filtered way—more like I've been getting 8 hours of sleep and green juice every day (spoiler: I haven't). Bonus points for the SPF 50. High protection and skincare benefits? Yes please. Murad, thank you for thinking of those of us who want to protect our skin without smelling like sunscreen at the beach. Is it a little pricey? Sure. But for what it delivers, I call it a glow-vestment. If your skin is tired of heavy SPFs and wants something that actually multitasks, this one's worth the hype. 10/10, already recommended it to three friends and a stranger at Ulta.
Murad always knocks it out of the park - consistently good formulas at an accessible price range. This one packs a punch and actually faded my dark spots. Would repurchase. The scent is mild as well.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] I recently tried the Murad Superactive Moisturizer with SPF 50, and while it has some really nice qualities, my experience ended up being a bit of a mixed bag. First off, the product applies smoothly and feels rich on the skin, though it's a little thicker than some sunscreens I've used. It wears well under makeup and I didn't experience any pilling, which is always a plus. Overall, it's comfortable to wear and doesn't interfere with my makeup routine. However, I decided to run a little experiment to test its sun protection. I applied a generous amount of the Murad sunscreen to one hand and my usual sunscreen to the other, then went outside with UV detection stickers on both hands. Unfortunately, I was really disappointed by the results. Despite layering a second coat of the Murad sunscreen, it didn't seem to provide sufficient protection—the UV exposure on both hands was pretty much the same. In the end, while the Murad Superactive Moisturizer SPF 50 feels great on the skin and works well under makeup, its actual sun protection doesn't seem to measure up based on my experiment. For anyone looking for reliable sun defense, I'd recommend considering other options.
